# Teemo Attacking.

@example Strikes at 3, 10 and 12 poison 3..6, 10..13 and 12..15. Seconds 12 and 13 are shared, so 3..6 and 10..15 are poisoned: 4 + 6 = 10.
[3,10,12]
4
=> 10

@example The first strike poisons 4, 5 and 6, just before the second strike, which adds 7, 8 and 9 of its own.
[4,7]
3
=> 6

@example The two strikes in second 9 poison the same seconds; in all, 1..3 and 9..12 are poisoned.
[1,9,9,10]
3
=> 7

# A single strike of one second.
[0]
1
=> 1

# duration 0 poisons nothing, however many strikes there are.
[0,0,3,8]
0
=> 0

# Every strike in the same second.
[6,6,6,6,6]
9
=> 9

# Strikes duration - 1 seconds apart share one second.
[2,6]
5
=> 9

# Strikes duration + 1 seconds apart leave one second free between them.
[2,8]
5
=> 10

# A strike at second 0 and one right after it: both seconds count.
[0,1]
1
=> 2

# duration 1: each different second with a strike counts once.
[3,3,4,9,10,10,11]
1
=> 5

# Shared, touching and separate seconds in one series.
[1,2,5,9,13,14,30]
4
=> 21

# The last strike at the largest time, with the largest duration: its
# seconds run far past 10^7.
[10000000]
10000000
=> 10000000

# The largest answer: two touching strikes of the largest duration.
[0,10000000]
10000000
=> 20000000

# 250 strikes 40000 seconds apart, each lasting 10^7 seconds: strikes
# times duration is past 2^31 - 1, though the answer is not.

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[5,6,10,13,16,19,22]
5
=> 22

@gen 2 small
[4,6,8,8,8]
0
=> 0

@gen 3 small
[2,6,7,12,15,19,19,23]
3
=> 19

@gen 4 small
[4,6,11,15]
4
=> 14

@gen 5 small
[4,8,12,16,19,20]
2
=> 11

@gen 6 small
[1,3]
5
=> 7

@gen 7 small
[1,1,5,6,8,12]
2
=> 9

@gen 8 small
[2,8,12,12,18,20,26]
4
=> 22
